content.title: Texas vs Purdue basketball: Replay, highlights as Boilermakers beat Horns on buzzer-beater
content.text: SAN JOSE, Calif. — For the first time in the NCAA Tournament, it wasn't Texas basketball making the biggest shot of the game.Purdue’s Trey Kaufman-Renn converted a missed shot by Braden Smith with .6 seconds left on the clock to lift the Boilermakers to a 79-77 win at the SAP Center. The basket pushed No. 2 Purdue (30-8) into the West Region championship against either Arkansas or Arizona, and it ended a stirring run for No. 11 Texas (21-15), which had used late baskets to beat North Carolina State, BYU and Gonzaga in the earlier rounds.Texas Longhorns forward Nic Codie (10) defends against Purdue Boilermakers forward Trey Kaufman-Renn (4) in the first half of Texas’ 79-77 loss to the Purdue Boilermakers in the Sweet 16 round of the NCAA Basketball Tournament at the SAP Center in San Jose, California, March 26, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman)But the Longhorns don’t enter the offseason with their heads hanging after winning three NCAA Tournament games and taking powerhouse Purdue to the wire.Advertisement“We played at a very, very high level the last couple of weeks (and) gave ourselves a chance to compete for a Final Four,” said Sean Miller, who completed his first season as Texas' coach. “Watching us kind of evolve and grow through the year, it has never been easy for us ever, and there were so many different times through the season where it looked like, man, if they don't get this next one, they're in trouble. We just found a way to get that next one or stayed the course.”MORE: Texas vs Purdue: Reaction to Longhorns' last-second loss to Boilermakers in Sweet 16It almost seemed like Texas would continue its course into the Elite Eight. Senior Tramon Mark shook off a twisted ankle and scored 29 points, his high mark in two seasons as a Longhorn. Fellow senior Jordan Pope added 12 points despite playing on what he revealed afterward as a broken foot. Junior forward Dailyn Swain added 15 points, including a driving and-one layup that tied the game 77-77 with 11 seconds left.But that left enough time for Purdue to convert on its final possession. Miller said he kept big man Matas Vokietaitis on the bench for the final possession because Purdue’s post, Oscar Cluff, had already fouled out and the Boilermakers had a smaller lineup.AdvertisementThe threat of Purdue All-American guard Braden Smith switching onto Vokietaitis worried Miller, so we went with guard Chendall Weaver against Smith. Weaver got the stop, but Kaufman-Renn rode Swain under the basket and got the tip in for the win.“By playing quicker or smaller, we could switch that and really defend the drive in a better fashion, because Matas can't really switch," Miller said. “You can't put Matas on Braden Smith on a switch. Look, we did get the stop. They got us with their size on the offensive rebound, and many times a game is won and lost not on the first shot, but on the second. We could have done a better job of blocking out.”Kaufman-Renn led Purdue with 20 points, and Smith ended with 16 points and five assists.MORE: Texas basketball photos: Longhorns take on Purdue Boilermakers in Sweet 16 matchupAdvertisementGOLDEN: Texas isn't a Cinderella, the Longhorns were just late to the ballRead below for a replay and highlights from Saturday as the Texas Longhorns lost to the Purdue Boilermakers in a third-round March Madness game. Purdue will play either No. 4 Arkansas or No. 1 in a West Regional final Saturday in San Jose, Calif.Texas Longhorns center Matas Vokietaitis (8) defends against Purdue Boilermakers center Oscar Cluff (45) in the first half as Texas plays Purdue in the Sweet 16 round of the NCAA Basketball Tournament at the SAP Center in San Jose, California, March 26, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman)Texas basketball vs Purdue scoring updatesFinal: Purdue 79, Texas 77 Trey Kaufman-Renn tips in a miss by Braden Smith with .4 seconds on the clock, and No. 2 Purdue survives.:11.9 2H: Purdue 77, Texas 77 Dailyn Swain drives to the bucket, takes the contact and fifth foul from Oscar Cluff, and ties the game with an and-one. There's another late clutch play from Texas. Purdue will have a chance to win it in regulation.Advertisement:21.5 2H: Purdue 75, Texas 72 Jordan Pope misses a 3, but Texas gets the jumpball call. The Longhorns have had late clutch shots in all three of their tournament games; do they have another in them?:39.5 2H: Purdue 75, Texas 72 Braden Smith, the 6-foot PG for Purdue, beats the 6-8 Nic Codie to the rim for a layup. He's All-American for a reason.:59.5 2H: Purdue 73, Texas 72 A follow by Texas guard Chendall Weaver cuts the Boilers' lead to one point.1:33 2H: Purdue 72, Texas 70 This may come down to free throws: Purdue is 12-of-16 and Texas is 5-of-12.3:56 2H: Texas 70, Purdue 70Cam Heide has fouled out in this Sweet 16 heavyweight fight. He's been very physical all game. And Tramon Mark (29 points, 11-of-13) has been very good all game with his highest-scoring outing in two years as a Longhorn. Texas needs to clutch up at the line, though; it's just 5-of-11.Advertisement7:39 2H: Texas 65, Purdue 63Tramon Mark has matched his Texas high with 26 points, and Dailyn Swain is up to 10 points after tying the game with a driving basket. Neither team blinking in this Sweet 16 matchup.10:20 2H: Texas 59, Purdue 58 Texas takes the lead after an earlier basket by Jordan Pope is a 3-pointer. Oh, and Tramon Mark's 24 points is a season high.10:20 2H: Texas 58, Purdue 58 Matas Vokietaitis draws his fourth foul of the game with 12:43 to go, so he'll have to sit for a while. Vokietaitis has been quiet this game with seven points and one rebound. Tramon Mark (24 points) and Braden Smith of Purdue (10 points, 5 assists) have engaged in a personal duel these last few minutes.Advertisement15:37 2H: Texas 49, Purdue 45 Cam Heide nails a 3-pointer, and Texas has surged ahead in the second half. One thing to watch: Tramon Mark turned an ankle on a 3-point attempt and he's limping around.16:45 2H: Texas 44, Purdue 43 This game has gotten very physical and very chippy. The Longhorns are skirting the line on some of their physical play, and I think Sean Miller likes it. But he doesn't like a third foul call on Matas Vokietaitis. Tramon Mark is up to 17 points on 7-of-9 shooting.19:36 2H: Purdue 39, Texas 38Tramon Mark (15 points) hits a transition 3 for Texas, and we're off in the second half.AdvertisementHalftime: Purdue 39, Texas 35 Both teams are showing off their prolific offenses. The Boilermakers are shooting 53.1% from the floor and outrebounding Texas 18-13. Fletcher Loyer has a game-high 13 points, but Trey Kaufman-Renn has been a real hero with 12 points on 6-of-6 shooting. Tramon Mark (12 points) leads a Texas team shooting 48.3% from the floor, and the Longhorns have been especially deadly from the arc (6-of-16).1:03 1H: Purdue 37, Texas 35 Jordan Pope buries a 3 from the corner for Texas and is up to nine points. What a gritty effort for Pope, a Bay Area native playing on a banged-up ankle.Advertisement3:13 1H: Purdue 30, Texas 30 Matas Vokietaitis swings an elbow while trying to corral a rebound, and he picks up his second foul. It may be a flagrant, much to the chagrin of Texas coach Sean Miller.6:45 1H: Purdue 28, Texas 25 Texas has cooled off a bit, but the Boilers have made four of their last five shots. Dailyn Swain is scoreless and 0-for-2 from the field; let's see if Sean Miller draws something up for his leading scorer on the season out of this timeout.9:39 1H: Purdue 24, Texas 23 If you like offensive basketball, hang this in whatever Louvre they have in an Indiana cornfield or a Harlem playground. Texas is shooting 60% and is 4-of-9 from 3-point range. Purdue is shooting 55%. But things a little too pretty for the Boilers after Braden Smith drives to the basket for a layup, and Sean Miller takes a timeout.Advertisement10:48 1H: Texas 20, Purdue 18 Tramon Mark is the story of the game for Texas early. The senior guard has 10 points on 4-of-5 shooting; teams need heroes at this time of year, and Mark has picked up the cape.10:48 1H: Texas 20, Purdue 18 Texas coach Sean Miller said that he would play a big lineup with Nic Codie and Matas Vokietaitis together, and Codie is already in the game for Texas in place of Cam Heide. And Simeon Wilcher will make an early sub for Jordan Pope, who's a bit ginger in his movements but does have a bucket. Rollicking start for both squads, who have blown through the first media timeout.Advertisement19:38 1H: Purdue 3, Texas 0Fletcher Loyer nails a 3 from the corner for Purdue, and we're off in San Jose.Texas basketball vs Purdue starting lineupsTexas Starting LineupPOS#NAMEGPPPGRPGAPGG0Pope,Jordan3513.12.11.9G12Mark,Tramon3513.53.51.9F3Swain,Dailyn3517.47.53.5F5Heide,Camden345.92.60.6C8Vokietaitis,Matas3515.77.20.7Purdue Starting LineupPOS#NAMEGPPPGRPGAPGG0Cox,C.J.378.52.61.3G2Loyer,Fletcher3714.12.32.0G3Smith,Braden3714.33.59.0F4Kaufman-Renn,Trey3514.18.52.6C45Cluff,Oscar3710.57.51.8Texas basketball vs Purdue injury report: Latest on Jordan PopeIn the final player availability report, Texas point guard Jordan Pope is listed as questionable and will be " a true game-time decision," according to a source close to the team. Pope led Texas with 17 points in its upset win over Gonzaga Saturday in a second-round matchup but injured his ankle late in the game. Texas forward Lassina Traore, who hasn't played since a Feb. 3 win over South Carolina, is officially out. Purdue guard CJ Cox, who hyper-extended his knee in the Boilermakers' win over Miami in the second round, is questionable.Advertisement No. 11 Texas (21-14) vs No. 2 Purdue (29-8): How to watch What: NCAA Tournament Sweet 16 gameWhen: 6:10 p.m. ThursdayWhere: March 26, 2026, at the SAP Center in San Jose, Calif.TV/radio: CBS; 1300 AM, 98.1 FMLine: Purdue is favored by 6½; total of 148½Reach Texas beat reporter Thomas Jones via email at tjones@statesman.com.
